# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 2
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "tell us those things which are to come"
- **EMET:** "tell us those things which are to come"
- **LOGOS:** "tell us what is to come"
- **PNEUMA:** "tell us what is coming"
- **Note:** Minor condensation across agents. EMET's "those things which" is more wooden/literal.

### v.2 — "great garden" vs. "vast garden"
- **EMET:** "great garden"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** vary between "great" and "vast"
- **Note:** The Ethiopic *'abiy* means great/large. "Vast" (PNEUMA) is an interpretive expansion; "great" is more literal.

### v.3 — "ancient man" vs. "aged man"
- **EMET:** "ancient man"
- **LOGOS:** "aged man"
- **PNEUMA:** "ancient man"
- **Note:** Significant: "ancient" could imply a primordial figure; "aged" simply means old. The text identifies him as Moses, so "aged" is more appropriate.

### v.3 — "shining in whiteness" vs. "gleaming in whiteness" vs. "blazing white"
- **EMET:** "shining in whiteness"
- **LOGOS:** "gleaming in whiteness"
- **PNEUMA:** "blazing white"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "blazing" adds intensity not in source. EMET's "shining in whiteness" is most literal.

### v.4 — Absence of "I do not understand" framing
- **EMET:** Phrases as a series of questions.
- **LOGOS:** Same.
- **PNEUMA:** Prefixes with "Lord, I don't understand."
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "I don't understand" before the questions — not in source text.

### v.6 — "Moses and the law"
- **EMET:** "he is Moses and the law which God gave him"
- **LOGOS:** "he is Moses, and the law which God gave him"
- **PNEUMA:** "He is Moses. He represents the law"
- **Note:** PNEUMA splits into two sentences and adds "represents" — interpretive paraphrase. The text equates the man with Moses; whether he also "is" the law is a separate question.

### v.7 — Description of children
- **EMET:** "who were not full-grown"
- **LOGOS:** "who had not yet grown to full age"
- **PNEUMA:** "before they reached the age when sin becomes possible"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's addition ("the age when sin becomes possible") is a theological interpretation not present in source text.

### v.8 — "on the left" vs. "at his left"
- **EMET:** "on the left"
- **LOGOS:** "on his left"
- **PNEUMA:** "at his left"
- **Note:** Minor preposition disagreement. "On his left" (LOGOS) is slightly more precise.

### v.9 — "for some have sinned and some have not sinned"
- **EMET:** "for some have sinned and some have not sinned"
- **LOGOS:** "for some have sinned and some have not"
- **PNEUMA:** "Because some sinned and some did not."
- **Note:** PNEUMA moves explanation to new sentence. LOGOS elides "sinned" in second clause. Minor.

### v.12 — "fasting to God" vs. "fasted unto God" vs. "fasted"
- **EMET:** "fasting to God"
- **LOGOS:** "fasted unto God"
- **PNEUMA:** "Some fasted."
- **Note:** PNEUMA drops "unto God" — loses the dative of religious direction. EMET's "to God" is unusual but literal.

### v.14 — "glory without end" (PNEUMA addition)
- **EMET:** "the kingdom and the honor and the glory which God has prepared for them"
- **LOGOS:** "the kingdom, the honor, and the glory that God has prepared"
- **PNEUMA:** "a kingdom, honor, and glory without end"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "without end" — not in source. Also drops the relative clause "that God has prepared for those who have feared him," losing the important qualifier.

---
*11 disagreements recorded. SOPHIA resolutions: "aged man" (v.3); retain "unto God" framing (v.12); retain full relative clause (v.14).*
